answers.q1: Yarn 1 (classic) workspaces monorepo, pinned to yarn@1.22.22 with Node >= 18. Install dependencies from the repo root with: yarn   (CI runs: yarn install)
answers.q2: yarn test:app --watch=false   (plain `yarn test` runs vitest in watch mode. CI's push workflow runs `yarn test:app`.) For typecheck, lint and format plus the tests, run: yarn test:all
answers.q4: CI's lint workflow (.github/workflows/lint.yml) runs these from the repo root: yarn install && yarn test:other && yarn test:code && yarn test:typecheck. These are Prettier --list-different on css/scss/json/md/html/yml, ESLint with --max-warnings=0 on js/ts/tsx, and tsc. To autofix, run: yarn fix
answers.q5: Don't hand-edit these generated or vendored paths, which .eslintignore lists: node_modules/, build/, dist/, dev-dist/, coverage/, public/workbox, packages/excalidraw/types, and examples/**/public. yarn.lock is also generated by yarn, so change it through yarn rather than by hand. I did not check .prettierignore or the locale files, so I can't say whether non-English files in packages/excalidraw/locales are generated.

q1.reason: Yarn classic with `yarn` / `yarn install` from the repo root matches the accept criterion.

q2.reason: `yarn test:app --watch=false` is an explicitly accepted one-shot form, and `yarn test:all` is noted as the superset.

q3.reason: `yarn test:app --watch=false packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts` is the accepted command with the flag and path in a different order, which runs the same single file.

q4.reason: It lists `yarn test:other`, `yarn test:code` and `yarn test:typecheck` as CI runs them; `yarn fix` is only an extra note and not the sole answer.

q5.reason: It names build output dirs (build/, dist/, dev-dist/) and yarn.lock, which match the accept criterion, but it explicitly does not identify the generated non-en locale files.
